lines.text: Decades later, there was less time for words and more space for laughter, hugs with no reason,
loud voices so our hearts can be overheard. My mind drifts into the darkness of our afterlives,
and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding our glasses of burning sands
and known journeys, and grateful to every living tree in the forest for the shared years
and the shared memories. This is brotherhood. Smiles with no reason,
narrow differences so our hearts can be overheard. Decades later, we can place our ears upon the next
brother's soul and follow paths of hilltops and canyons, of blinding lights and infinite nights,
all too familiar and create the type of space for laughter
and football and recollections that bring us home every time.

passage.line: and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding our glasses of burning sands
passage.why_fulcrum: The hinge from the empty rooms of the dead to 'We are all here': the reunion becomes the living holding burning sand. After it, the gratitude, brotherhood and laughter all mean time running out.

answer.title: The National Institutes of Health
answer.said: So I think we're holding our own.
answer.why: Echoes 'we are all here, each holding our...' in plain speech: holding our own means still standing against the odds, which is what the burning sand asks of the friends.
